card werk-mc-open  [decided]
Shift+click forks and goes there. A plain click still navigates.
why: Both gestures land on the card you clicked. The only difference is whether a new conversation starts there.

Eryk decided this, and reversed the earlier recommendation of a background fork. See #werk-mc-open:opt1.

## The three gestures

    click              the map goes there. This conversation follows, as today.
    Shift+click        a fork rooted at that card, focused. The map goes there too.
    Shift+click again  on a card that already has a tab: switches to it. It does not fork twice.

Both gestures move the view to the card you clicked. That is one rule, not two. The difference between them is only whether a new conversation starts there.

Nothing is added by the fork moving the view: it follows from #werk-mc-follow. Focusing a tab moves the map to that tab's card, and the fork's card is the one under the cursor. So this card does not introduce a navigation rule; it just says the fork is focused rather than backgrounded.

## Why the throughput is not lost

Leaving a conversation does not pause it. The turn you started in tab A keeps running while you are in tab B. That is the feature. What you give up by focusing the fork is the ability to *read* A while B starts, and that is worth one keypress — Cmd+1, see #werk-mc-keys.

## Second entry point

A '+' at the end of the tab strip forks at whatever card is open. Same operation, no card link needed, and the map does not move because you are already there.

Rejected: a plain click opening a tab by default (#werk-mc-open:opt0). It taxes the gesture Eryk uses most.

`#werk-mc-open` has no subcards — nothing refines it in the map.

It does depend on four cards: `#werk-mc-fork`, `#werk-mc-tabs`, `#werk-mc-follow`, `#werk-mc-keys`. Since `#werk-mc-open` depends on it, that staleness has propagated here too.
